column1: # `dungeon-mode.md §8.1`'s Klimb row for a two-way ladder, whose three
# literals had no reader until today: `Klimb-U/D-` "when both directions
# are available (it blocks until up or down is chosen, and Space answers
# `Pass\n\n` and climbs nothing)", then `Up!` or `Down!` printed "first,
# before any test".
# The party stands on the Deceit two-way ladder at level 3, seeded with
#   seed_position <profile> dungeon=33 level=3 x=1 y=1
# In order: K and Space (the pass, which climbs nothing), K and Down, and
# then K and Up to come back. The level label in the viewport's top border
# is the independent check that the two climbs went where they say.
# This is a lottery from the `pass` beat onward. `dungeon-mode.md`'s Wandering
# monsters section: dungeon mode keeps a single active monster per level,
# stepped toward the party by a "randomized greedy move" every turn, and a
# step that lands it adjacent launches combat and prints `Attacked[ from the
# <dir>]!` without an explicit Attack. The two sides never share that walk's
# random stream, so a run long enough to hold several `wait`s can have the
# original's active monster close and interrupt with its own combat transcript
# while this engine's dungeon stays quiet (or the reverse) - measured
# 2026-10-12, where the original was attacked mid-script and the two
# viewports parted for the rest of the run. The `lit` and `prompt` beats,
# which is what this scenario pins (the Klimb-U/D- literals), agreed on both
# runs; a divergence from `pass` onward must be re-run before it means
# anything.
# Where the monster comes from, traced 2026-10-16: the seed's active-monster
# record is all zeros - live (the empty marker is all ones), stamped level 0,
# at `(0,0)`, combat class 0, the Mage - and a load *reuses* it whole
# (`dungeon-mode.md §4.1`). It walks level 3 from `(0,0)` through `(0,1)` onto
# the party, which is why stock's line is always `Attacked from the west!`:
# 4 of 13 stock runs (2026-10-12 22:06 and all three of 2026-10-16). This
# engine gated the monster on its stamped level and was attacked in none until
# that gate was removed (`dungeon_loaded_monster_record_walks_the_party_level_*`
# test); headless after the fix it was attacked in 6 of 10. Still a lottery -
# the walk's direction draws - but now one both sides can draw.
# requires-seed: the party standing on a Deceit two-way ladder, with a torch
